proposal: Congress should abolish the CFPB and reverse Dodd-Frank Section 1061, returning its functions to the banking regulators and the FTC. If the Supreme Court affirmed the Fifth Circuit funding ruling, the President should order the agency dissolved, withdraw its rules and guidance, return staff to their prior agencies and the building to GSA. Interim steps for Congress include sending unspent civil penalty money to Treasury, repealing Section 1071, tying enforcement to APA rulemaking, letting respondents elect an Article III forum, and defining unfair, deceptive and abusive practices.
remaining: An act of Congress repealing Dodd-Frank Title X (or Section 1061) and reassigning CFPB functions to banking regulators and the FTC

status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 the CFPB still exists and no statute abolishing it was found; a 2025 reconciliation law lowered its funding cap to 6.5 percent of Federal Reserve operating expenses, the Bureau withdrew a set of guidance documents (2025-05-12), and a final rule published 2026-05-01 narrowed rather than repealed the Section 1071 small-business lending rule (effective 2026-06-30, compliance from 2028-01-01). The administration's attempt to cut staff is the subject of NTEU v. Vought: a preliminary injunction (2025-03-28) was vacated by a divided D.C. Circuit panel (2025-08-15), rehearing en banc was granted (2025-12-17), and on 2026-06-19 the en banc D.C. Circuit granted a limited remand in No. 25-5091, holding the appeal in abeyance and retaining jurisdiction, so the district court can decide whether to modify, suspend or dissolve the injunction in light of a revised plan, filed 2026-03-31, to cut about 53 percent of staff; in July 2026 the acting director paused that plan so a successor could decide and the district judge granted a joint motion for a partial stay, with the injunction against mass layoffs remaining meanwhile. Brian Johnson, nominated as director in early June, was advanced by the Senate Banking Committee on a party-line vote on 2026-09-17 with no floor vote scheduled, and reports conflict on whether Mark Paoletta (from 2026-08-01, per Consumer Finance Monitor) or Russell Vought is acting director. Three courts have rejected the Justice Department's narrow reading of the Federal Reserve funding statute (a D.D.C. clarification of 2025-12-30, an N.D. Cal. ruling reported 2026-03-20, and a District of Oregon opinion of 2026-09-25 that vacated the decision not to request fiscal year 2026 funding but declined injunctive relief for that year), and the chapter's condition for presidential dissolution did not occur, since on 2024-05-16 the Supreme Court upheld the Bureau's funding mechanism and reversed the Fifth Circuit in CFPB v. Community Financial Services Association of America.

timeline.event: After NTEU and co-plaintiffs sued on 2025-02-13 (NTEU v. Vought, D.D.C.), Judge Amy Berman Jackson grants a preliminary injunction preserving CFPB staff, contracts, data and operations while the case proceeds.
CFPB publishes a Federal Register withdrawal of interpretive rules, policy statements and advisory opinions (scope not reviewed beyond the title).

A divided D.C. Circuit panel (Katsas, Rao; Pillard dissenting) vacates the 2025-03-28 preliminary injunction in NTEU v. Vought (No. 25-5091) and remands: the majority holds the employee organizations' firing claims belong in the Civil Service Reform Act review scheme, that the APA claims fail for lack of a discrete final agency action, and that the statutory claims do not qualify as ultra vires or constitutional claims for equitable review; the dissent would affirm because Congress created the Bureau and its mandates. The opinion does not rest on irreparable harm.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

timeline.event: The D.C. Circuit orders rehearing en banc in NTEU v. Vought (No. 25-5091): a majority of eligible judges voted to rehear the case, the order vacates the court's 2025-08-15 judgment, leaves the April 2025 partial stay pending appeal in effect, and sets argument for 2026-02-24. On 2025-12-30 Judge Jackson clarifies that the district court's injunction requires the CFPB to keep requesting Federal Reserve funding (per the ABA Banking Journal).
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

timeline.event: Consumer Finance Monitor reports that Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) granted summary judgment to Rise Economy, Woodstock Institute and the National Community Reinvestment Coalition, holding the Office of Legal Counsel reading of Fed 'combined earnings' as profits unlawful and ordering the Bureau to keep requesting funds each quarter (the ruling date is not stated in the article).

CFPB final rule on small business lending data under Regulation B narrows rather than repeals the Section 1071 requirements (higher lender threshold, lower small-business revenue cutoff, fewer data points), effective 2026-06-30 with compliance from 2028-01-01.

The en banc D.C. Circuit, in a per curiam order in No. 25-5091, denies a motion to modify the stay pending appeal, grants a limited remand for the district court to decide in the first instance whether to modify, suspend or dissolve the preliminary injunction in light of the CFPB's revised reduction-in-force plan and other developments, and holds the appeal in abeyance while retaining jurisdiction; four judges would have waited for the en banc ruling. Judge Jackson's minute order of 2026-06-22 records the remand and sets filing dates of 2026-06-25 and 2026-07-02. (Source: the D.C. Circuit order on media.cadc.uscourts.gov.)
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia

timeline.event: Scotsman Guide reports that the acting director paused the plan to cut staff from 1,174 to 556 so a successor can decide, that Judge Jackson granted a joint motion for a partial stay, and that Brian Johnson was nominated in early June to replace the acting director.

A Federal Register notice of interagency rescission of the 2022 interagency statement on special purpose credit programs is signed for the CFPB by Mark Paoletta as 'Chief Legal Officer' (not as acting director); the Bureau's regulatory agenda notice of 2026-08-14 lists reconsideration of the Section 1071 and Section 1033 rules and no rulemaking to move or end Bureau functions.
The Senate Banking Committee advances Brian Johnson's nomination as CFPB director on a party-line vote; a floor vote is not scheduled.

In State of New York v. Vought (D. Or., No. 6:25-cv-02384-AA), Judge Ann Aiken grants the plaintiffs' motion for partial summary judgment, reads 'combined earnings' in the Dodd-Frank funding provision as the Federal Reserve's gross revenues without deduction of expenses, vacates the Director's decisions that funds cannot be requested when the Federal Reserve's interest expenses exceed its income and not to request fiscal year 2026 funding, declares those decisions contrary to law, and declines injunctive relief for fiscal year 2026 because that year was nearly over. It is the third court ruling against the Justice Department's narrower reading of the funding statute.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon

uncertainties: The D.C. Circuit's 2025-08-15 panel opinion, its 2025-12-17 en banc order and its 2026-06-19 limited remand order were read (the last re-opened on the courtlistener storage host in this pass; it leaves to the district court whether to modify the injunction, asks to be notified promptly, and sets motions on future proceedings within 21 days of the district court's decision), as were the district court's 2026-06-22 minute order (docket page) and the Supreme Court's 2024 funding decision. The 2026-03-31 filing date and 53 percent figure for the revised plan come from Banking Dive, not the court order. The July 2026 partial stay and the paused plan rest on Scotsman Guide; the joint filing (ECF 184) and a 2026-07-10 minute order described by an external retrieval were not opened (copies only on trade-site and blog hosts, which are not used), and no later district court order and no en banc decision after the 2026-02-24 argument were found in a court document. The third funding ruling is the District of Oregon's Opinion and Order of 2026-09-25 (Doc. 86), read on a Justia copy with the date taken from the signature block; the trade report of 2026-09-30 is a later report date. That opinion dates the N.D. Cal. Rise Economy ruling 2026-03-13 and says it is on appeal to the Ninth Circuit (No. 26-3134); the timeline keeps 2026-03-20, the date of the trade report, because the Rise Economy order itself was not opened. The date the 2025 reconciliation law was signed is not given in the Banking Dive source. On the acting director, a Federal Register notice published 2026-08-25 is signed for the Bureau by Paoletta as Chief Legal Officer, which neither confirms nor contradicts either report. No bill to abolish the CFPB, Civil Penalty Fund change or enforcement-forum change was searched for beyond the sources named.
